security_audit.summary: I confirmed the eval example as a high-risk pattern because it evaluates user-provided expressions inside a function tool. The remaining static findings are documentation fences, placeholder secrets, benign URLs, or validation text without executable reconnaissance or credential disclosure. No prompt injection or hidden exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md or scripts/verify.py.

remediation.issue: Unsafe eval in calculator tool example
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval(expression) with a whitelist parser such as ast plus explicit arithmetic operators, or remove the calculator tool from production scaffolds.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API key setup can be copied into shared files
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to set OPENAI_API_KEY through local secret storage and never commit real keys to source control.

remediation.issue: Weather tool sends user-supplied city names to an external service
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party request, validate city input, set timeouts, and allow users to disable the tool.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable patterns for OpenAI Agents SDK projects. This skill provides scaffolds for agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and FastAPI integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains Agent and Runner setup with async, sync, and streaming examples.
Shows function tool patterns, including typed tools and async HTTP tools.
Demonstrates handoffs and agents-as-tools orchestration for specialist agents.
Provides input and output guardrail examples for tutoring workflows.
Includes FastAPI endpoint and streaming response integration patterns.
Includes a verification script for required skill documentation sections.
limitations: Provides examples and scaffolding guidance, not a complete generated application.
Requires users to verify current OpenAI Agents SDK APIs before production use.
Contains an unsafe calculator example that must be replaced before deployment.
Does not cover non-SDK frameworks such as LangChain.

use_cases.title: Prototype a tutoring agent
use_cases.description: Create a Python tutor with clear instructions, practice flows, and basic tool use.

use_cases.title: Add specialist routing
use_cases.description: Design triage and handoff patterns for concepts, debugging, and exercise generation agents.

use_cases.title: Review agent safety patterns
use_cases.description: Use guardrail examples to plan validation, refusal, and testing behavior for agent workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build my first OpenAI Agents SDK assistant for <task>. Include the Agent setup, Runner pattern, and the smallest local test.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tool Calling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate agent with one safe function tool.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a function tool to my agent for <capability>. Use typed inputs, validation, and safe error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Agent Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-agent handoff workflow for <domain>. Define triage rules, specialist responsibilities, guardrails, and expected handoff tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Production Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced service integration with operations concerns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold a production-ready FastAPI service around an OpenAI Agents SDK workflow. Include streaming, tracing, environment configuration, and security review steps.

output_examples.input: Create a Python tutor with concept, debug, and exercise specialists.
output_examples.output: A scaffold plan with a triage agent, three specialists, routing rules, guardrail checks, and local test prompts.

output_examples.input: Add a documentation search tool to an agent workflow.
output_examples.output: A tool design with typed input, structured result fields, validation steps, and guidance for safe error handling.

output_examples.input: Create a streamed support assistant for FastAPI.
output_examples.output: A service outline covering streamed runner events, response handling, trace configuration, and endpoint testing.

best_practices: Replace unsafe evaluation examples with validated parsers before production use.
Keep API keys in environment or secret storage, and never commit real credentials.
Test handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and tool errors before exposing an agent endpoint.
anti_patterns: Do not copy the eval-based calculator example into production code.
Do not expose raw tool errors or trace details directly to end users.
Do not add broad network tools without validation, timeouts, and clear user consent.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps scaffold OpenAI Agents SDK projects with agents, tools, handoffs, guardrails, streaming, and FastAPI examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and examples that developers adapt to their own project.

faq.question: Is the calculator example safe for production?
faq.answer: No. Replace the eval-based expression handling with a validated parser or a restricted arithmetic tool.

faq.question: Does it cover multi-agent workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes handoff routing and agents-as-tools examples for specialist orchestration.

faq.question: What should I verify before deployment?
faq.answer: Verify SDK compatibility, secret handling, tool validation, network behavior, guardrails, streaming, and trace visibility.
